producer_checks.novelty: First Japanese Q3 GDP estimate and China’s October activity release; compares investment and consumption, then separates trade exposure from local-currency input costs and financing.
producer_checks.bilingual_parity: Same 17 source URLs and chart data in both locales.
producer_checks.visual_evidence: Two explicit quantitative charts sourced to China NBS and Japan ESRI, two evidence/scenario tables, a causal flow and a regional exposure map.

limitations: Japan’s GDP release is preliminary and the quarterly headline rounds to negative zero.
China’s retail and trade series are nominal and the industrial value-added figures are real. The fixed-asset investment window is January through October.
Market readings are intraday and gathered at different times. No Brazilian market close, new Focus or IBC-Br outcome is used.
contrary_evidence: China’s nominal goods imports increased despite weak retail and property investment.
Japan’s non-residential business investment grew despite declining household consumption.
Cheaper crude in dollars may bring limited relief in reais when the dollar appreciates.

en.title: Global Macro — China’s factories expand, Japanese consumption falls and the dollar raises adjustment costs
en.deck: October’s Chinese data show strength in advanced manufacturing and weak retail growth. In Japan, business investment rose as household spending fell.
en.regime: Concentrated industrial growth and weakening consumption alongside expensive dollar funding.
en.key_risk: Trade, commodity and credit effects diverge as supplier exposure and funding terms vary.
